description:
Medium-sized deciduous tree, 16-27 meters tall, with a trunk up to 2 meters in diameter and a broad, rounded crown. The nark is smooth and greenish-white to greyish-white with diamond-shaped dark marks on the young trees, becoming blackish and fissured toward the base of older trees. Young shoots and buds are covered with whitish-gray wooly pubescence.

Leaves 4-15 cm. long, roughly 5-lobed, with a thick layer of whitish down on undersides and less thick on the upper part of the leaf.

Trees are dioecious; flowers emerge in hanging catkins up to 8 cm. long, produced in early spring, which give way to small dehiscent capsules that ripen and burst open in late spring, distributing abundant cottony-tufted seeds in a way similar to the native Populus trichocarpa.

Trees introduced from Europe and planted throughout the Sun Lakes campground and along the shores of several lakes within the park.

The back of the leaf is fuzzy and pale white.

There are several very large trees of this kind in the River Trail park by the Missouri River in Great Falls.  Beautiful!
